title: Red team compliance dry-run notes
content:
Context: quick red-team style dry run to exercise SOC2-ish control evidence collection and identify awkward edges for Dedicated/Private customers. Not formal audit; purpose is to find gaps and figure out low-effort evidence grabs.

Top-level objective:
- Validate that we can produce traceable evidence for a subset of controls within 48 hours (small team).
- Surface common misunderstandings about responsibilities (eng vs platform vs infra ops).

Scope (short):
- Focus on: access provisioning (oncall/SSO), change control for runtime config, incident logs/alerts, backup verification, and model deployment approval path.
- Exclude: full pen-test, HR payroll controls, physical office security.

Assumptions / constraints:
- Using hosted API + Dedicated for simulated customer. Some artifacts live in cloud provider (GCP) and we may need IAM exports.
- Timebox: 6 engineer-hours per control.
- Some evidence will be replaced with screenshots and tracebacks for the dry run.

Quick control mapping (first-pass, very rough):
- Access provisioning -> evidence: Okta change logs, group membership export, onboarding ticket in Jira. (check: retention of audit logs > 90d?)
- Change control -> evidence: PRs + merge approvals, deployment runbook + canary rollout logs (Console traces).
- Incident response -> evidence: PagerDuty incident timeline export, postmortem draft, Slack thread.
- Backup & recovery -> evidence: snapshot list, SRE restore runbook, test restore result (s3-object count diff).
- Data encryption -> evidence: KMS key policy, kms audit logs, HSM integration note.

Red-team style scenarios to simulate quickly:
1) Unauthorized dev access hypothesis: simulate a user added to project group then removed; confirm audit trail is tamper-evident. Steps: add test account in Okta sandbox, request resource access, escalate, then remove; collect logs.
2) Emergency rollback: push a bad config to dedicated runtime, trigger auto-fallback, validate alert flow and rollback evidence in console.
3) Data restore check: delete small test dataset, run restore playbook, time-to-restore and integrity check.

Evidence collection checklist (practical):
- Export commands / links to the raw logs (don’t just screenshot): 
  - Okta: System Log export (CSV) + query used
  - GCP: auditLogs filter string and timeframe
  - PagerDuty: incident export CSV ID
  - Redwood Console: route-level latency/cost trace link + tracing span id
- Take a short screencast for multi-step console evidence (10–60s)
- Record exact commit hashes + PR numbers for code/config changes

Observed friction & notes (from run):
- Console trace links are ephemeral; need standard permalink pattern for evidence. If only ephemeral, capture trace JSON.
- Team seldom tags PRs with control IDs — add a tiny template to PR description: "Control: <ID> (e.g., C-CCA-03)"
- Some infra logs are aggregated under infra-monitoring project; permission to export is gated to infra-admins (bottleneck). Try short-lived service account?

Open questions / follow-ups:
- What retention windows do auditors expect for Okta vs cloud logs? Current default: 90 days for app logs, 365 for core? Need to confirm. -> ACTION: ask Security for canonical retention table (Marina).
- Are model artefacts (weights, artifacts) considered part of backup controls for Private deployments? Might be separate control. -> ACTION: sync with Applied ML (Noah).
- How to generate a canonical evidence bundle (zip + manifest) that maps items to control IDs? Idea: use a small script that builds manifest.json (control -> list of artifact filenames). Worth prototyping.

Low-effort quick wins to pursue:
- Add small PR template snippet for control tagging (1h).
- Add a Console permalink exporter that saves trace JSON to GCS and returns stable link (2-3d feature).
- Run a weekly 1h "evidence capture" rotation for infra-admin to pre-export recent logs (15m job).

Notes to self:
- Keep the dry-run friendly for engineers — make artifacts easy to produce (single-command where possible).
- Document the scope of each evidence item in Confluence page TRUST-210.

Sample rough script commands (for my notes):
- Okta: curl -H "Authorization: SSWS ${OKTA_TOKEN}" "https://{{org}}.okta.com/api/v1/logs?filter=..." > okta-log.csv
- GCP: gcloud logging read 'resource.type="k8s_container" AND protoPayload.methodName:"google.cloud"' --project infra-monitoring --limit 1000 --format json > gcp-logs.json
- PD: pd incidents export --since 2026-02-01 --until 2026-02-20 --output incidents.csv (check CLI flags)

Immediate next steps (today):
- Run scenario 1 in sandbox account (Marina) and capture Okta log row + screenshot.
- Open a tiny RFC for permalink exporter and assign to developer-experience backlog (Ava).
- Draft evidence bundle manifest example and attach to Confluence stub (linked above).

Random scribbles / brainstorm hooks:
- Could we embed a "control header" into PR checklists that automatically attaches PR -> control mapping to the release artifact?
- Lightweight CI job that collects artifacts when a tag/release is created and zips into a canonical archive for auditors.

End scratch — save and iterate after PD export completes.

References (for later cleanup):
- Confluence stub: TRUST-210 (todo: expand)
- Slack thread: #trustrun-2026 (pinned messages)
- Related ticket: JIRA SEC-412 (perms export bottleneck)
- GH PR example: repo/redwood-infra/pull/987 (demo of PR tag)

-- Marina
